This project contains synthetic data and analysis created for demonstration purposes only.
:::

## Load the data

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)

data_file <- "data/synthetic-coffee-sales.csv"

# Synthetic data is not committed to Git (see .gitignore) — generate it if missing
if (!file.exists(data_file)) {
  source("data/generate_data.R")
}

sales <- read_csv(data_file, comment = "#")
```

## Revenue by store

```{r}
#| label: store-table
sales |>
  group_by(store) |>
  summarise(cups = sum(cups_sold), revenue = sum(revenue)) |>
  arrange(desc(revenue)) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(cups, decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_currency(revenue, decimals = 0) |>
  cols_label(store = "Store", cups = "Cups Sold", revenue = "Revenue")
```

## Monthly cups sold by drink

```{r}
#| label: monthly-trend
#| fig-height: 4
monthly <- sales |>
  mutate(month = lubridate::floor_date(date, "month")) |>
  group_by(month, drink) |>
  summarise(cups = sum(cups_sold), .groups = "drop")

ggplot(monthly, aes(month, cups, color = drink)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cups sold", color = "Drink",
       title = "Cold Brew climbs as the weather warms") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
```

## Key takeaway

Cold Brew starts the year as the slowest seller and finishes as the top drink by June.
